summary: Generalize resilience rule in AGENT_SYSTEM prompt to remove task-specific tool names and grader-gaming heuristics.

edits.hypothesis: Replacing specific tool references ('roi_crop') and grader-derived heuristics ('prioritize positive signal') with general principles of skepticism toward negative consensus when targeted inspection fails reduces leakage while preserving the core resilience mechanism.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The failure mode is a reasoning bias encoded in the system prompt; removing specific task-level details requires editing the prompt text itself, not just control flow.
edits.trigger_condition: Always active for M-arm agents receiving the AGENT_SYSTEM prompt.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000009, the agent previously ignored a positive expert finding due to negative consensus; the generalized rule still encourages prioritizing specialized positive signals without hard-coding the specific 'roi_crop' failure. (preservative) Tasks where all models agree are unaffected as the rule only triggers on disagreement/failure. (transfer) Generalizes to any domain where high-resolution/specialized tools fail and generalists provide conflicting negative consensus.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal; the change removes specific biases and tool names, making the instruction more robust and less prone to overfitting to the current toolset.
edits.mechanism: Replacing specific tool references ('roi_crop') and grader-derived heuristics ('prioritize positive signal') with general principles of skepticism toward negative consensus when targeted inspection fails reduces leakage while preserving the core resilience mechanism.
